subject: Culture
title: The Gap Year
description: A fast breakdown of The Gap Year for builders.

hook.text: British and Australian students invented the gap year—a year off between school and university to travel.

buildup.text: The tradition borrows from the Grand Tour, when 18th-century aristocrats traveled Europe to 'complete' their education.

discovery.text: Gap years often follow predictable routes: Southeast Asia, South America, Australia. It's a structured adventure.

twist.text: Critics call it 'poverty tourism.' Wealthy students visit developing nations without lasting contribution.

climax.text: The gap year is a modern walkabout—a privileged version of the ancient quest for self outside the familiar.

punchline.text: The destination teaches less than the departure.

quiz.question: What 18th-century aristocratic tradition is the gap year descended from?
